target: area:iwasawa (part 2 of 3): ColemanPowerSeries, DirichletPadicLFunctions, EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture, IntegralIwasawaTheory, LocallyAnalyticDistributions, PadicHodgeRegulators, PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras, SpecialValuesBirchTate
summary: Six findings, all of them about what the area does not plan rather than about what it plans wrongly. Five are mathematics that an accepted paper route asks a named layer of this area to own and that no layer of the atlas plans: the p-adic Gamma function with the Gross-Koblitz formula; the Ferrero-Greenberg theorem; the Fontaine-Messing-Kato log-syntomic package; the Dasgupta-Kakde character-group-ring and quadratic-presentation algebra; and the derived finite-slope theory for perfect complexes of Banach modules. The sixth is a duplication: the cyclotomic main conjecture for abelian fields over Q is an endpoint of both EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture L3/L4 and IntegralIwasawaTheory I.5, by two different proofs, with no import between them and no restructuring proposal resolving it. The mechanical checks came back clean: every `requires` in the area resolves, the stage graph has no cycle, the one backticked Mathlib declaration in the area's descriptions exists at the pin, and the layers of other roadmaps that use characteristic ideals cite the owner rather than rebuilding it. Disclosure: this session reviewed two of the fourteen paper extractions routed into the area (PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-25, issue #1307, and PAPER-PILLONI-20, issue #1327). No finding below rests on either; finding 5 cites PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21 and -25, which this session did not touch.

findings.where: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 (and the roadmap as a whole)
findings.claim: Morita's p-adic Gamma function and the Gross-Koblitz formula are planned by no layer of the atlas and are absent from both pinned libraries, although an accepted, reviewed paper route asks this roadmap to own them.
findings.evidence: PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18 (Dasgupta-Kakde-Ventullo, On the Gross-Stark Conjecture, Ann. of Math. 188 (2018) 833-870, doi 10.4007/annals.2018.188.3.3) routes three missing items to DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 on a source route whose reason reads: 'The p-adic Gamma function, the Gross-Koblitz formula and the Ferrero-Greenberg theorem are the inputs to the case F = Q, which motivated the conjecture. They belong with the Kubota-Leopoldt p-adic L-functions of a rational base; L3 already owns the branches, Iwasawa's logarithm and Leopoldt's p-adic formula.' The items are 'The p-adic Gamma function' (locator: section 1, p. 836; statement: 'Morita's p-adic Gamma function Gamma_p : Z_p -> Z_p^* is the unique continuous function with Gamma_p(n) = (-1)^n prod_{0<j<n, p not| j} j for every integer n >= 1') and 'The Gross-Koblitz formula' (same locator). L3's description in data/atlas.json plans the Teichmuller branches, log_p with log_p(p)=0, the complex formula for L(1,chi), Leopoldt's formula for L_p(1,chi) and the pole on the trivial component; it does not mention Gamma_p or Gross-Koblitz, and neither does any other stage: a text search over all 1968 stage descriptions for 'Gross-Koblitz' and for a p-adic Gamma function returns nothing. At the pinned commits the libraries have neither: the shared declaration index has no padicGamma and no GrossKoblitz, and grep over the Mathlib and Tau Ceti checkouts finds only the real, incomplete and multivariate Gamma functions.
findings.fix: Give DirichletPadicLFunctions L3 ownership of Morita's Gamma_p (existence, uniqueness by continuity, the two functional equations Gamma_p(x+1) = -x Gamma_p(x) on units and -Gamma_p(x) on pZ_p) and of the Gross-Koblitz formula in the form the source states it, with the choice of pi with pi^{p-1} = -p and zeta_pi = 1 + pi mod pi^2; L3 already owns the Gauss sums and the branch/logarithm theory that Gross-Koblitz relates. If L3 is judged full, add a sixth layer L5 to the same roadmap with L3 as its prerequisite.

findings.where: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 (and the roadmap as a whole)
findings.claim: The Ferrero-Greenberg theorem, the derivative formula for the Kubota-Leopoldt p-adic L-function at s = 0, is planned by no layer of the atlas, although the same accepted route asks this roadmap to own it.
findings.evidence: The third item of the same source route in PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18 is 'The Ferrero-Greenberg theorem' (locator: section 1, p. 836): 'let F = Q and let chi be an odd Dirichlet character with chi(p) = 1, the exceptional case r_p(chi) = 1. Then L_p'(chi omega, 0) is expressed explicitly through the values log_p Gamma_p(a/f), 0 < a < f, of the p-adic Gamma function, where f is the conductor of chi.' A text search over all 1968 stage descriptions for 'Ferrero-Greenberg' returns nothing. The two stages that match 'Ferrero' are EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L4 and IntegralIwasawaTheory:L4, and both are about the different theorem of Ferrero-Washington (the vanishing of mu); IntegralIwasawaTheory L4 is titled 'Abelian Leopoldt and Ferrero-Washington'.
findings.fix: Own the Ferrero-Greenberg formula in DirichletPadicLFunctions L3, immediately after Leopoldt's formula for L_p(1,chi), which is the analogous explicit evaluation and which L3 already plans; it depends on finding 1, since its right-hand side is a sum of log_p Gamma_p(a/f). State the exceptional hypothesis chi(p) = 1 explicitly, and keep the nonvanishing consequence separate from the formula.

findings.claim: The classical Fontaine-Messing-Kato log-syntomic package - the sheaves S_n(r)_X, the period morphism to p-adic nearby cycles, the small-twist isomorphism for i <= r <= p-1 and the syntomic exponential - is planned by no layer, while an accepted paper route asks D.2 to own it and an accepted restructuring proposal keeps D.2 out of that scope.
findings.evidence: PAPER-COLMEZ-NIZIOL-17 (Colmez-Niziol, Syntomic complexes and p-adic nearby cycles) routes four missing items to PadicHodgeRegulators:D.2: 'The log-syntomic sheaf S_n(r)_X' (section 1.1.1, p. 2), 'The Fontaine-Messing-Kato period morphism' (same, 'Fontaine-Messing and Kato construct period morphisms alpha^FM_{r,n} : S_n(r)_X -> i^*Rj_*Z/p^n(r)'), 'The classical small-twist isomorphism' (equation (1.3), pp. 2-3, 'For i <= r <= p-1 the period map ... is an isomorphism'), and 'The syntomic exponential alpha_{r,i}' (p. 3). The route's own reason says 'This paper supplies the semistable logarithmic form of the same objects'. D.2's description in data/atlas.json plans 'a syntomic regulator in the exact smooth/unramified settings used here', 'filtered de Rham complexes, Frobenius data and the syntomic mapping fibre' and a comparison of regulators; it plans neither log structures nor a period morphism. The accepted restructuring proposal RS-26 fixes that boundary: its entry for PadicHodgeRegulators:D.2 is 'keep', with the reason 'Keep the exact smooth/unramified syntomic and etale regulator comparison'. No other stage plans the objects either: a text search over all 1968 stage descriptions for 'Fontaine-Messing' returns nothing, and of the 26 stages that mention 'syntomic', those in PrismaticCohomology (PR.4, PR.5, PR.8) build the prismatic Nygaard/Tate-twist theory and its logarithmic extension, not the Fontaine-Messing-Kato complexes or their period map.
findings.fix: Add a layer to PadicHodgeRegulators that owns the log-syntomic complexes S_n(r)_X for a log-smooth scheme over a henselian discrete valuation ring, the Fontaine-Messing-Kato period morphism to log p-adic nearby cycles, the small-twist isomorphism in the stated range i <= r <= p-1 (Kato, Kurihara, Tsuji) and the syntomic exponential; make it a prerequisite of D.2 and D.5, since D.5 already says the logarithmic input for bad or semistable reduction 'is not supplied by the unramified-field calculation'. If the atlas prefers to route this through the prismatic theory instead, then PrismaticCohomology PR.4/PR.8 must state the comparison with the Fontaine-Messing-Kato complexes explicitly and D.2 must import it; what is not tenable is that two accepted routes ask D.2 for it while RS-26 keeps D.2 to the unramified case.

findings.claim: The ring theory that the modern proof of the Brumer-Stark conjecture runs on - character group rings, quadratically presented modules and their Fitting ideals, the higher adjugate identity, and the involution # - is planned by no layer, although an accepted paper route asks L6 to own it and IntegralIwasawaTheory I.6/I.7 plan the theorems that use it.
findings.evidence: PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-23 (Dasgupta-Kakde, On the Brumer-Stark conjecture, arXiv:2010.00657) routes thirteen missing items to PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6, among them 'Character group ring R_Psi' (section 2.2), 'Lemma 2.2: O[G]/(N I) is a character group ring', 'Quadratically presented module' (section 2.3), 'Lemma 2.4: order of a quadratically presented module over a finite index ring', 'Lemma 2.7: Fitting ideals of two extensions with a common quotient', 'Compound matrices and the higher adjugate identity' (section 3.4, proof of Lemma 3.9), 'Transpose is well defined up to projective summands' and 'The ring R^# and the involution # on character group rings' (section 6.1). L6's description plans commutative O-orders, the Gorenstein condition and its dual, self-injective Artinian quotients, exact duals on finite modules, Hom_R(-,R) versus O-linear and derived duals, Fitting ideals, projective presentations and exterior biduals; it does not mention character group rings, quadratic presentations, compound matrices or the involution #. A text search over all 1968 stage descriptions for 'character group ring', for 'quadratically presented' and for compound matrices or the adjugate returns nothing in this area (the three adjugate matches are in unrelated group-theoretic layers). Meanwhile IntegralIwasawaTheory I.6 and I.7, which plan the integral Brumer-Stark theorem, are named by 115 and 112 planned items of the same extraction, including 'Theorem 1.7(a): Sel_Sigma^{Sigma'}(H)_p^- is quadratically presented' and 'Theorem 1.7(b): Fitt_{Z_p[G]^-}(Sel) = (Theta^#)' - so the theorems are planned while the notions they are stated in are not.
findings.fix: Extend PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L6 to own the character group ring R_Psi of a finite abelian G and a set of characters, the quotient criteria of Dasgupta-Kakde Lemma 2.2 and Corollary 2.3, quadratically presented modules with the order and Fitting-ideal lemmas 2.4-2.7, the compound-matrix/higher-adjugate identity, the transpose up to projective summands and the involution # - all of it ring-level algebra of exactly the kind L6 already owns for Burns-Sakamoto-Sano. Record in I.6/I.7 that these notions are imported from L6, so that the Brumer-Stark statements are not the first place the notions appear.

findings.claim: The finite-slope theory for perfect complexes - compact endomorphisms of perfect complexes of projective Banach modules, derived finite-slope localization, and the Stein and quasi-Stein exhaustions it is stated over - is planned by no layer, although two accepted paper routes ask L4 for it and one of them says so in as many words.
findings.evidence: PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21 routes to LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L4 the item 'section 6.1.1: compact endomorphisms of perfect complexes of projective Banach modules' (locator: section 6.1.1, second paragraph, arXiv p. 139), and its route reason reads: "L4 is to 'Prove continuity and compactness ..., nuclear/Fredholm determinants in the precise compact-operator setting, slope decompositions, and compatibility with specialization on slope-adapted affinoids'. As the Pilloni (2020) extraction asks, it must add the complex setting (section 6.1.1, arXiv p. 139, and the proof of Theorem 6.3.16)." PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-25 routes five more missing items to L0/L3/L4, including 'Quasi-Stein exhaustion' and 'Stein exhaustion' (section 2.2.17, PDF p. 21) and 'Derived finite-slope localization' (section 4.6.46, PDF p. 93). L4's description plans the operator-level theory only: 'continuity and compactness of the semigroup operators used for modular symbols, nuclear/Fredholm determinants in the precise compact-operator setting, slope decompositions, and compatibility with specialization on slope-adapted affinoids'. A text search over all 1968 stage descriptions returns no occurrence of 'quasi-Stein', of 'compact endomorphism', or of perfect complexes of Banach modules; the three stages that mention slope decompositions are LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4 itself, OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O6 and IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.0, and none of them is about complexes.
findings.fix: Extend LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4 to the derived setting: compactness of an endomorphism of a perfect complex of projective Banach A-modules through a representative, the Fredholm determinant and slope decomposition of such a complex, the comparison with the module-level theory it already plans, and the Stein and quasi-Stein exhaustions over which the finite-slope localization is stated. Keep the solid-module formulation of the BCGP 2025 items out of this layer unless the atlas decides to own solid functional analysis; the compact-operator content is separable from it.

findings.claim: The cyclotomic main conjecture for abelian fields over Q is an endpoint of two roadmaps of this area, by two different proofs, with no import between them and no restructuring proposal resolving the ownership.
findings.evidence: EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3 ('Equality and the unconditional notes endpoint') plans: 'Prove equality in the preceding divisibility by the cyclotomic-unit index/class-number argument of Rubin III.2.8 and Lang's appendix ... Deduce ... char_(Z_p[[G^+]])(X_infty^+) = I(G^+) zeta_p for every odd prime p. This is the unconditional Theorem 13.8', and :L4 ('Abelian fields and p=2') plans 'Greither Theorem 3.2 and its p-ramified formulation ... In particular, include the case p=2 integrally', the roadmap summary naming Kolyvagin-Rubin as 'the route of record'. IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.5 ('Classical main conjectures at odd primes') plans: 'Prove the abelian-Q main conjecture of Mazur-Wiles, with the chosen algebraic module and p-adic L-function conventions. Prove Wiles's totally real main conjecture at odd primes. The proof programme includes Hecke algebras at the needed levels and weights, Eisenstein ideals, congruence modules, Galois representations and stable lattices, construction of the required class-group extensions, and both divisibilities of characteristic ideals.' Neither layer cites the other: I.5's requires are I.2 and I.3 only, and neither the four restructuring proposals that touch the area (RS-13, RS-14, RS-16, RS-26) nor RS-08 assigns an owner for the statement - the only entries naming EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture in RS-08 and RS-16 are stage-edge forwardings.
findings.fix: Decide the ownership in the atlas text rather than leaving it implicit. Either (a) name EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture L3/L4 the owner of the abelian-over-Q statement, have I.5 import it and keep I.5 for Wiles's totally real theorem and the Hecke/Eisenstein machinery that only the totally real case needs - which is also the endpoint SpecialValuesBirchTate B.4 consumes; or (b) keep both proofs deliberately, and say so in both layer descriptions, with one named the route of record and the other marked an independent second proof, so that a blueprint job does not build the Eisenstein-ideal programme twice by accident.
